newsitem.title: FINLAND: OPK CHIEF SEES NO DRAMA WITH 49 BANKS OPTING OUT.
newsitem.headline: OPK CHIEF SEES NO DRAMA WITH 49 BANKS OPTING OUT.

text.p: The chairman of Finnish cooperative banking group Osuuspankkikeskus-OPK said on Friday the new group would proceed according to plan even though 49 of its former members decided to opt out.
"A clear majority (228 member banks) has decided to join and we will proceed according to earlier plans," OPK chairman Antti Tanskanen told Reuters after a news conference.
"It is those that remain outside that will have to re-evaluate their position," he added.
Tanskanen said the 49 banks staying outside the new cooperative accounted for roughly 10 percent of clients and of the end-1996 balance sheet of the group, formerly Osuuspankkien Keskusliitto OKL.
Final decisions on participation were still pending from 21 banks and Tanskanen said the door was open for them to join the new group.
"I expect these 21 banks to make their final decision within the next few weeks," Tanskanen said.
He did not expect any of the "outsider" banks to rejoin the group.
Tanskanen did not fear fierce competition from the 49 outsider banks as they operate in different localities.
The name of the new cooperative will be Osuuspankkikeskus-OPK (OPK).
